title: On Balance, To What Degree is Burr's Conjecture True?
summary: For many trees $T$, the Ramsey number of $T$, denoted by ${\mathcal R}(T)$, is determined by the sizes of the partition classes in its unique bipartition. In 1976, Burr proved that when $T$ has partition classes of size $t_1$ and $t_2$ with $t_1 \le t_2$, the Ramsey number is at least $\max(2t_2-1,2t_1+t_2-1)$, and conjectured that this is tight. While counterexamples have been found for some pairs $(t_1, t_2)$, a main focus of research on this problem has been determining ratios $t_2/t_1$ or bounds on the maximum degree of $T$ for which Burr's bound is either exactly or asymptotically…
